headline: UK fiscal watchdog pairs an uncertain AI productivity forecast with early adoption and sector data
summary: The Office for Budget Responsibility’s October 2026 outlook retains its uncertain central assumption that AI will add 0.2 percentage points a year to UK productivity growth by the medium term. It reports that 30% of businesses said they used AI in September 2026, up from 15% two years earlier, and describes faster recent output-per-worker growth in some AI-associated sectors. The ONS identifies the adoption estimate as a voluntary survey result and official statistic in development, with a 25.7% response rate. The OBR cautions that sector growth was broad-based and short-period measures volatile. These are a forecast and descriptive observations, not evidence that AI caused an economy-wide productivity gain.
